insight.title: You Destroy Your Memories by Thinking About Them
insight.subtitle: Every time you recall an event, you rewrite the data.

sections.text: Every time you think about a childhood memory, you are accidentally destroying the truth of what actually happened. Your brain doesn’t hold steady images; it recreates scenes from scratch, introducing permanent errors.
You aren't remembering the original event from years ago. You are remembering the version you conjured up the last time you told the story. The truth fades with every single retelling.
Two people can experience the same wedding but recall opposite details years later. Your brain isn't opening a file; it performs a script that changes with every new audience.
You are remembering a story, not a life.
